question: Since 2021, Germany has had a national fuel emissions trading scheme in place, which served as a model for the European ETS2. For companies which fall outside the EU ETS1, the German Fuel Emissions Trading Regulation (BECV) introduced a national CO2 emissions leakage compensation mechanism. As state aid, the BECV is subject to review by the Commission for compliance with state aid rules.

An initial list of eligible sectors, mostly ETS1 sectors, was approved on 8 August 2023. A procedure to include additional sectors not covered by ETS1 was launched immediately thereafter. This procedure has now been ongoing for almost two years. According to the German authorities, the Directorate-General for Competition (DG COMP) has been in possession of all the necessary data for more than two years.

The companies concerned have therefore been waiting for several years for the possibility to apply for relief, which is proving increasingly problematic in light of rising CO2 costs and intense international competition. 1.
What steps has the Commission taken since the submission of the complete data, and what factors have led to the delays?

How does the Commission take into account existing protection instruments under the EU ETS1 when examining national mechanisms, and how does the Commission ensure a timely examination of national transitional instruments, such as the BECV, to prevent competitive disadvantages, in particular for SMEs?
In the context of the announced revision of the ETS State Aid Guidelines, are adjustments planned to expedite and increase the transparency of such procedures?
answer: While the Commission cannot share detail, it can confirm to the Honourable Member that it is in close and constructive contacts with the German authorities on the extension of the compensation scheme in the context of the national Fuel Emissions Trading Regulation (BECV) in Germany. The BECV is a national system, which was taken into account in the mentioned Commission decision of 10 August 2023 (1).
As it is not part of the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS), it could not be part, either, of the amendment of the ETS State aid guidelines, adopted on 23 December 2025 (2).

State Aid SA.63191 (2023/N) — Carbon leakage compensation in the context of the German fuel emission trading system. Communication from the Commission amending the Guidelines on certain state aid measures in the context of the system for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading post-2021, C(2025) 9298 final.
